safety-rules.title: 5 essential safety rules for beginners
safety-rules.excerpt: Before you jump or roll — the basics for every session.

body.heading: 1. Always progress gradually
body.text: Start on the ground, then very low heights.

body.heading: 2. Check the spot
body.text: Make sure the surface is dry and stable.

body.heading: 3. Don't train alone at first
body.text: Having someone else helps in an emergency.

body.heading: 4. Listen to your body
body.text: Pain is a signal — stop immediately.

body.heading: 5. Avoid dangerous places
body.text: No damaged buildings. We do not list them.

body.heading: Why safety matters most
body.text: Parkour is not about jumping from high roofs. The goal is body control. Every injury keeps you from training.

body.heading: Safety rules
list: Always progress gradually: start on the ground, then very low heights.
Landing first: learn a quiet landing before any jump.
Check the spot: dry, stable surface.
Listen to your body: pain is a signal — stop.
Avoid dangerous places: no damaged buildings.

what.safetyText: Parkour is a sport that requires gradual training. Do not attempt advanced moves before mastering the basics.
what.intro: Parkour is an art and philosophy of moving efficiently from point to point using only the body. The goal is not showmanship, but overcoming obstacles safely and intelligently.
what.originBefore: It was born in France in the late 1980s through
what.originAfter: , inspired by his father Raymond Belle. The philosophy: “Be strong to be useful.”
what.syriaFocus: In Syria we focus on a safe version suited to local reality — especially in Damascus.
whyList: A friendly community that encourages gradual progress
what.dangerText: Like any sport. Most injuries come from rushing. With safety and gradual progress it can be practiced safely.

faqs.a: From 12–14 with supervision; adults at any age.
Shoes with good grip and comfortable clothes. No other gear needed.

faqs.q: Where do I train in Damascus?

faqs.a: Yes. Parkour Syria is affiliated with Parkour.com and works within its vision to support the local parkour community in Syria.
